title: ChainSpace: A Chained-Reasoning Paradigm for Spatial Intelligence
claim: Isolated question accuracy can overestimate ability; chained questions need preserved state to stay consistent, which local-cue answering lacks.
layout: 3 regions: video strip on top, chained questions left, two robot panels right
description: The top of the figure is a film strip of five frames from an apartment video. Frame 3 is highlighted, with colored boxes around a fireplace and a black sofa. Below it, on the left, a gray box titled "Chained Questions" holds three linked multiple-choice questions about direction relative to an @-shaped ornament. Curved arrows connect the questions. Key phrases are colored to match the highlighted objects and the frames. On the right are two panels. Panel (a), "Local-cue-based answering (Frame 3)", shows black robots with speech bubbles B, C, C. The first answer has a green check and the next two have red crosses. Panel (b), "Reasoning with preserved spatial state (Frames 1-5)", has a pink border and pink robots answering B, D, B, all with green checks. The contrast of checks against crosses draws the eye first.
caption: Illustration of the ChainSpace paradigm. Given a video trajectory, spatial questions are organized into a logically constrained chain, where later questions depend on spatial constraints established in earlier rounds. (a) A model following an independent-QA behavior may answer an early question correctly using local cues from a single frame, but fail on later questions that require preserving and updating spatial state. This illustrates why isolated question accuracy can overestimate spatial intelligence. (b) By reasoning with the preserved spatial state across frames and question turns, the model can produce answers that remain jointly consistent throughout the chain.
abstract: Spatial intelligence requires foundation models to maintain coherent spatial state across interactions with the physical world. However, existing data-centric approaches typically treat spatial reasoning as independent question-answer instances, enabling shortcut-based answering and providing limited supervision for persistent spatial understanding. To address this, we introduce ChainSpace, a chained-reasoning paradigm that structures spatial reasoning as a state-preserving multi-round process. In this paradigm, spatial questions are organized into logically constrained and jointly consistent chains, where later questions depend on spatial constraints established in earlier rounds. Following this principle, we instantiate ChainSpace-Bench, a manually annotated real-world multi-round benchmark with a Chain-Aware Metric, and ChainSpace-Pipeline, a simulator-based chain-structured supervision generation framework for spatial intelligence training. Experiments show that ChainSpace-Bench exposes chain-level failures that are not captured by isolated question accuracy. Additionally, with a relatively small amount of simulator-generated chained data, models trained by ChainSpace-Pipeline achieve the best performance among open-source models on ChainSpace-Bench and transfer competitively to multiple external spatial intelligence benchmarks. These results establish ChainSpace as an effective paradigm for more faithful evaluation and more data-efficient learning of spatial intelligence.
